# Tokyo Family Trip Plan: 2026-07-10 to 2026-07-12

A kid-friendly 3-day Tokyo itinerary for **2 adults + 2 children (ages 7 and 10)**, designed to keep each day under **18,000 JPY** for attractions and food combined. I’ve kept transit between activities short, chosen mostly central Tokyo neighborhoods, and added one indoor backup each day for July heat or rain.

## 3-Day Family Schedule with Budget and Backup Plan

| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | Est. Spend |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-10 | Ueno Park + Tokyo National Museum grounds walk | Asakusa: Senso-ji, Nakamise snacks, rickshaw-free stroll | Sumida River area + early dinner near Asakusa | **14,000–17,500 JPY** |
| 2026-07-11 | Odaiba Seaside Park + DiverCity plaza | teamLab Planets area or Joypolis-style indoor fun | Toyosu/ Odaiba dinner and waterfront walk | **15,000–18,000 JPY** |
| 2026-07-12 | Shinjuku Gyoen early visit | Harajuku: Yoyogi Park + Takeshita Street | Tokyo Station / Marunouchi lights + simple dinner | **13,500–17,000 JPY** |

## Day-by-Day Family Itinerary

### Day 1: Ueno and Asakusa Classics
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Start at **Ueno Park** for an easy stroller-free walk, playground time, and a relaxed museum exterior visit.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/31/2014_02_08_ueno.jpg Alt=Morning: Start at **Ueno Park** for an easy stroller-free walk, playground time, and a relaxed museum exterior visit, Tokyo, Japan
- Afternoon: Head to **Asakusa** for **Senso-ji Temple** and Nakamise shopping street; keep it light with snacks, souvenirs, and photos.
- Evening: Walk the **Sumida River** promenade, then have an early dinner in Asakusa with kid-friendly tempura, curry rice, or udon.
- Indoor backup: **Tokyo National Museum** family-friendly galleries or a nearby shopping arcade if the weather turns hot or wet.
- Transit note: Ueno to Asakusa is a short ride; all moves stay well under 90 minutes.

### Day 2: Odaiba Waterfront Fun
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Begin at **Odaiba Seaside Park** for open space, bay views, and a calm start before the heat builds.
Media: Alt=Morning: Begin at **Odaiba Seaside Park** for open space, bay views, and a calm start before the heat builds, Tokyo, Japan
- Afternoon: Choose one indoor anchor: **teamLab Planets** if tickets fit the budget, or a lower-cost indoor arcade/mall option around **DiverCity**.
- Evening: Do an easy waterfront dinner near **Aqua City** or **DiverCity**, then a short night walk for skyline views.
- Indoor backup: **Miraikan-style science museum visit** or extended mall time with play areas and food courts.
- Transit note: Odaiba stays compact, so the whole day is easy on kids and adults.

### Day 3: Shinjuku, Harajuku, and Central Tokyo
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Shinjuku Gyoen** early for cooler temperatures, open lawns, and a peaceful family walk.
- Afternoon: Move to **Harajuku** for **Yoyogi Park** and a short, lively pass through **Takeshita Street** for crepes and snacks.
- Evening: Finish at **Tokyo Station / Marunouchi** for lights, a simple dinner, and an easy departure-friendly location.
- Indoor backup: **Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observatory** or a shopping center play stop if you need shade and air-conditioning.
- Transit note: Shinjuku to Harajuku to Tokyo Station is a practical central-Tokyo loop with short rides.

## Budget-Friendly Family Notes

- Keep attraction choices to a few paid entries only; most of this plan uses **parks, temple areas, and waterfront walks**.
- For meals, target **1 casual lunch + 1 simple dinner + snacks**, which keeps the family total near the budget cap.
- Best money-saving food picks: **udon, curry rice, onigiri, tempura bowls, ramen, and convenience-store fruit/yogurt**.
- July in Tokyo can be hot and humid, so plan outdoor time **early morning and after 4:30 PM** when possible.
- For children ages 7 and 10, this route works well because each day mixes **movement, one major highlight, and a flexible indoor fallback**.
